the organizational change led to a new representation of the identity of teacher-educators that was accepted by the majority of the participants.
teacher educators’ identity representations are affected by organizational change, but that the change does not lead to a new identity.
the participants in the study adopted new representations of the role of a teacher-education faculty member, yet few of them perceived themselves as researchers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the tension between the social and personal levels of identity.
the tension between the organizational change that took place and the personal identity of teacher-educators.
the ways in which teacher educators perceive themselves as researchers, and the extent to which these perceptions are congruent with the new organizational culture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
participants accepted the organizational change but were unable to fully internalize it.
the participants’ representations are not consistent with their actual practices and that their identity perceptions do not reflect their actual practices.
the change was not fully internalized by participants and was not reflected in their personal identities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, while participants accepted the new representation of teacher-education, they did not fully internalize it.
, although the organizational change was accompanied by a change in the representation of teacher educators’ identity, this change was not reflected in their personal identity.
the participants’ identities were transformed in response to the organizational change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizational change can be effective in transforming social representations, yet the process of identity change can be long and arduous.
, despite the fact that the organizational change was imposed on the faculty, it was accepted by the participants and became a part of their social reality.
, although organizational change is a necessary condition for identity transformation, it is far from sufficient.
